examples.solution_text:
The right angles match $A\leftrightarrow D$, and the $60^{\circ}$ angles match $C\leftrightarrow E$. The remaining vertices match $B\leftrightarrow F$.
$\triangle ABC\sim\triangle DFE$
The corresponding sides are $AB$ and $DF$, $BC$ and $FE$, and $CA$ and $ED$.
$\angle BCA$ corresponds to $\angle FED$.

The single arcs match $J\leftrightarrow R$, and the double arcs match $K\leftrightarrow S$. The remaining vertices match $L\leftrightarrow T$.
$\triangle JKL\sim\triangle RST$
Side $JK$ corresponds to side $RS$.

Match the endpoints of the sloping sides: $A\leftrightarrow P$ and $B\leftrightarrow Q$. Follow the adjacent sides around each boundary: $C\leftrightarrow R$, $D\leftrightarrow S$, $E\leftrightarrow T$.
$ABCDE\sim PQRST$
Side $CD$ corresponds to side $RS$.
$\angle EAB$ corresponds to $\angle TPQ$.
Matching sides and boundary order distinguish the vertices even where angles repeat.

Consider the two triangles separately.
$\angle KOL=\angle POQ$ (vertically opposite angles).
$\angle OKL=\angle OPQ$ (alternate angles on parallel lines).
Thus $K\leftrightarrow P$, $O\leftrightarrow O$ and $L\leftrightarrow Q$.
$\triangle KOL\sim\triangle POQ$
The corresponding sides are $KO$ and $PO$, $OL$ and $OQ$, and $KL$ and $PQ$.

The angle at $D$ is shared.
$\angle DGH=\angle DEF$ and $\angle DHG=\angle DFE$ (corresponding angles on parallel lines).
The vertices match $D\leftrightarrow D$, $G\leftrightarrow E$ and $H\leftrightarrow F$.
$\triangle DGH\sim\triangle DEF$
Side $GH$ corresponds to side $EF$.

examples.derivation: The right angles give A↔D; the marked 60° angles give C↔E; hence B↔F. Therefore triangle ABC is similar to triangle DFE. Corresponding sides are AB–DF, BC–FE and CA–ED, and angle BCA corresponds to angle FED. The coordinates give matching right triangles with scale factor 1.5, with the marked angles approximately 60°.

Single arcs give J↔R and double arcs give K↔S, leaving L↔T. Therefore triangle JKL is similar to triangle RST, and JK corresponds to RS. The coordinate transformation (x,y)↦(7−1.3x,1.3y) maps every first-triangle vertex to its stated counterpart and preserves the marked angles.

The reflected reduction (x,y)↦(7−0.7x,0.7y) maps A,B,C,D,E to P,Q,R,S,T respectively. Thus ABCDE is similar to PQRST; CD corresponds to RS; angle EAB corresponds to angle TPQ. Adjacent side relationships and boundary order support the correspondence despite repeated angles.

Both crossing intervals pass through O, and KL and PQ are vertical and parallel. Vertically opposite angles match KOL with POQ; alternate angles match OKL with OPQ. Hence K↔P, O↔O and L↔Q. Triangle KOL is similar to triangle POQ, with KO–PO, OL–OQ and KL–PQ corresponding. Multiplication of coordinates by −1.5 maps K to P and L to Q.

G and H are the midpoints of DE and DF, and GH is parallel to EF. The shared angle at D and corresponding angles give D↔D, G↔E and H↔F. Therefore triangle DGH is similar to triangle DEF, and GH corresponds to EF.
